title: saturated-window-allocator-and-real-time-util-inspector
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: spikes in tenant demand were causing inconsistent burst delivery and noisy utilization signals that confused the autoscaler. This PR introduces the Saturated Window Allocator (SWA) and a lightweight Real-Time Util Inspector (RTUI) to provide a stable, low-latency utilization signal and fair burst apportionment across tenants. Key goals: 1) bound worst-case headroom consumption during multitenant surges, 2) provide a smoothed utilization metric suitable for autoscaler decisioning, and 3) make degradation predictable and reversible with a safety fence. Design summary: SWA divides fleet headroom into short saturation windows and apportions micro-bursts to tenants proportional to their active share with a capped soft-lease; tenants that repeatedly exceed their soft-lease are recorded by RTUI and subject to an adaptive burst-throttle fence. RTUI samples per-pool GPU occupancy and queue latency at a 1s cadence and emits a 10s-window smoothed util_percent and burst_rate metric that downstream controllers can consume. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.saturated_window; opt-in experiments enabled for 5% of traffic for three days, then scoped to 20% while monitoring regressions. Includes a canary against the autoscaler where the new util_percent is compared against the legacy sampler for A/B evaluation. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is a no-op unless the feature flag is on; config keys are additive. Tests and validation: unit tests for allocator math and lease decay; integration job that runs synthetic burst patterns; staging cluster soak (72h) and a production canary observed for 48h before merge. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (internal/designs/swa.md) [x] unit tests [x] integration job [x] metrics and dashboards [x] staged rollout. Related work: references ENG-7212 (fair-burst-prober) and ENG-7420 (autoscaler-smoothing).
